title: iThink Big
metaTitle: iThink Big — School Assembly Website · Artifact Digital
description: A website for a live school assembly program: video-led, built around one action — book an assembly — and designed for school leaders reading it on a phone between classes.

card.blurb: A live assembly program translated into a site that moves like the show and books like a business.
card.imageAlt: Three phone screens from the iThink Big site over an audience of students at a school assembly.

titleLines.text: The website needed to catch up.

lede: iThink Big has been running motivational assemblies in schools since 2000 — a loud, live, deeply human hour in a gym full of students. The website had to carry that into a browser, and then make the next step obvious: book an assembly.
pillarsHeading: A live program, flattened into a web page.

pillars.title: The experience wasn't coming through
pillars.body: What happens in the room is music, story and a few hundred students paying complete attention. Written down as paragraphs on a conventional education site, it becomes a description of an assembly rather than a reason to book one.

pillars.title: Several audiences, one page
pillars.body: Principals, teachers, parents, youth pastors and partner organizations arrive with different questions, and none of them read the whole site. Each needed their answer within a screen or two of landing.

pillars.title: Decisions get made on a phone
pillars.body: School leaders look this up between classes, standing in a hallway. A site that only works on a desktop is a site that gets closed and forgotten.

storyParagraphs: The decision that shaped everything else was to lead with footage from real assemblies rather than a photograph of a building. The first thing a visitor sees is the room itself — the stage, the crowd, the moment — with the headline and the booking button sitting over it. Nothing has to describe the atmosphere, because you're already looking at it.

Underneath that, the page is disciplined. One primary action, Book an Assembly, repeats down the page and stays reachable in the mobile header. The organization's own record — students reached, years running, schools and districts served — is stated once, high up, in its own words, then left alone. Credibility comes from named references and the people who actually run the program rather than from adjectives.

Video hero sections usually break two things: legibility and accessibility. So the type sits on a controlled overlay that holds contrast wherever the footage goes bright, motion respects a reduced-motion preference, and every action is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus state. The energy is the point, but nobody has to fight it to find the phone number.

The structure then makes room for the parts of the organization that a single page usually buries: what the programs actually include, who the team is, the references schools ask for, and the work in Mexico, which gets its own place in the navigation rather than a paragraph at the bottom.
storyImageAlt: The iThink Big homepage on a laptop and a phone, with footage of a live assembly behind the headline.
storyCaption: Desktop and mobile share one hierarchy: what it is, who it’s for, and how to book.

highlights.title: A site that feels like the room
highlights.body: Real assembly footage leads, so the tone is set before anyone reads a word.

highlights.title: One obvious next step
highlights.body: Book an Assembly is the only primary action, repeated as the page moves and pinned within reach on mobile.

highlights.title: Legible over video, and keyboard-friendly
highlights.body: Controlled contrast over moving footage, visible focus states, and motion that respects a reduced-motion setting.

highlights.title: Room to grow
highlights.body: Programs, references, team and the Mexico work each have a home, so the site can expand without a redesign.
